In his 2001 testimony he dates and sources his own interest: 'In 1967 when I was at Westover Air Force Base, one night before going to bed I saw this light moving across the sky', hovering 'directly over the facility where they kept the nuclear weapons', watched for about ten minutes through a telescope, before it was 'out of sight in just a second or two'.

He states that he missed the Norton air show himself: 'the magazine Popular Science came back again and [told me] they had some really, really crazy deadline for another illustration', so 'I had to beg off on this air show'. His entire account of the exhibit is therefore what Sorensen told him 'the following week, after Brad got back home'.

claims.text: The Frank Carlucci identification is his own labelled speculation, and the earliest opened document describes a different kind of man. His 2001 testimony gives the host as 'a tall, thin, white-haired man with glasses [and] an Italian-sounding last name', 'already a millionaire in his own right and was in civilian life again after having been either a Secretary of Defense or an Under-Secretary of Defense', followed by 'this fellow whom I speculate was probably Frank Carlucci.' William B. Scott's 1990 interview notes instead record Sorensen describing his host as a man who 'was in the Carter administration, and they wanted him on the Bush team', who 'is a very organized, straightforward, honest, etc. guy. In fact, he's a Democrat, which is not in keeping with the Bush admin. at all', and who 'Runs a business of injection molding and special materials...has about 6 businesses.' Frank Carlucci was the sitting Secretary of Defense on 12 November 1988, so neither 'in civilian life again' nor the injection-moulding businesses fits him on that date.

The Disclosure Project's press conference of 9 May 2001 presented 20 of the 69 people whose interviews appear in Greer's book, and no opened source lists which 20. NOTHING OPENED PLACES MARK McCANDLISH AT THAT PODIUM, and his testimony in the Briefing Document is dated December 2000, five months before it. Appearing at section 3.8.5 of the April 2001 document and appearing at the May 2001 press conference are two different facts with two different records, and this board should never infer the second from the first. The same caution applies to every witness in this cluster.

conflicts: The Frank Carlucci identification is contradicted by the earliest opened document. The 1990 Scott notes describe a Carter-administration Democrat running about six injection-moulding and special-materials businesses; Carlucci was the sitting Secretary of Defense on 12 November 1988. The board's existing triage calls the identification 'a researcher's guess at two removes'; the opened record corrects that in one direction and confirms it in another, because the guess is McCandlish's own, published in 2001 in his own voice and labelled as speculation, and only afterwards re-attributed to researchers by later carriers.

His 2001 testimony adds a claim the 1990 document does not contain: 'Brad said that in this exhibit at Norton Air Force Base, a three star general said that these vehicles were capable of doing light speed or better.' The 1990 document says the opposite about ranks present: 'I did NOT see any stars in there--like generals of any sort. If there had, I would have noticed that.'

label: Mark McCandlish
narrative: Mark McCandlish is the origin point in print of a named craft, and he is not a witness to it. By his own account in the Disclosure Project's April 2001 Briefing Document he works principally as a conceptual artist for defence contractors, he missed the Norton Air Force Base air show of 12 November 1988 because of an illustration deadline, and everything he describes about a hangar holding three hovering saucer-shaped craft was told to him the following week by a friend who was there. He drew it, and the drawing is what propagates. The one contemporaneous document in the thread, an Aviation Week editor's unpublished 1990 interview notes, records the same direction of relay and records the witness disowning part of the drawing. He was declared deceased on 13 April 2021 at his home in Redding, California, of a gunshot wound to the head; the Shasta County coroner ruled suicide on an external examination that expressly declined an internal one. What makes him a node is proximity to the claim, not credibility: he held no office, no clearance is documented anywhere in the opened record, and his whole account is a relay of somebody else's sighting.
